scores.evidence: Set up ArgoCD or Flux for declarative deployments; Rollback via git commits
scores.rationale: Generic statements are mostly correct, but it lists oddities like DAST and database connection pooling under CI/CD scaling and never reaches hard technical areas.
It is a generic platform-build checklist that defers all service onboarding to weeks 34-52 and never surveys the 50 services' stacks or targets.

scores.evidence: Select CI/CD stack (Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, ArgoCD, etc.)
scores.rationale: The phases are recognizable, but no single design is chosen, and GitOps is recommended alongside pipeline deploy stages without reconciling the two.
Validation is generic. Nothing tests risky assumptions early, since the first real service is onboarded at week 34, and the success-metric targets are unjustified.
Assumptions about team size, cloud, stack and compliance are never stated. Discovery is listed as a task, yet the 52-week timeline is stated as fact.
Failure modes are mostly absent. It has only generic rollback and monitoring items and nothing on credential leaks, flaky builds or CI outages.
It covers monitoring, on-call, runbooks and rollback automation at a list level, with no named owner for the platform and nothing on changing templates safely.
It mentions spot instances, artifact cleanup and cost per deployment, but it comes late (weeks 27-30), with no volume estimates or runner-cost basis.
It lists choices but does not distinguish one-way decisions from reversible ones, and it commits to a full stack before any pilot.

It builds the full platform, including tracing, DAST, service mesh and distributed caching, for a year before any service uses it, which is speculative, and the per-service observability scope is irrelevant.
